analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: a new `--prompt-prep` benchmark row in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (patch at about line 572) and a new 'Prompt preparation and admission' table in docs/reference/configuration.md (hunk at lines 586-595). The cli-reference head text in units :10 and :11 is unchanged surrounding context, so I did not treat pre-existing content as new. No source or control code is changed, so no security control regresses in this PR.

The docs describe a source change not supplied here: a per-tokenizer prompt-piece token cache. It reuses token IDs for rendered chat-template pieces that were 'already seen in the request's prefix-cache scope', is on by default, and is disabled by the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. The same change adds linear-time rewrites of the Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS chat templates, background verification, and a 'cold load release' that lets later coordinator events overtake a request waiting for a model load.

Relevant threat models are T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT timing oracle, A-001), T-028 and T-053. The new in-memory cache is scoped by the cacheSalt-derived prefix-cache scope, which is consistent with T-041's account isolation. However, it introduces another potential same-account hit/miss timing channel, and it is not covered by T-041's affected_files or its mitigations. The implementation, including how scope is keyed, whether pieces are cleared on unload, and whether the piece cache holds plaintext prompt text in memory, was not supplied, so I cannot verify it.

The cold-load release reorders events in ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift. It could interact with T-053 (stale authorization, cancel and revocation ordering) and T-010 (cancellation), but the code is unseen.

The threat model needs updating. The next review should examine the source files PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift and ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift. It should check that the cache is keyed by cacheScope/account, that it is wiped on unload and KEK wipe, that the verification fallback fails closed, and that the work reordering preserves revocation and cancel handling.
